The only negative is fc1.bias at seed069 init, whose norm is .0017 against an allfour total of 5.14, so it carries no weight. Dot products are positive in all four states, so the regression term is not opposing the ranking term on this batch.\n\nWhat the vectors do show is magnitude, and it changes with training. Regression/ranking norm ratio on allfour:\n\n| State | reg norm | rank norm | ratio |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| 061 init | 4.63 | 0.61 | 7.6 |\n| 061 step128 | 1.01 | 0.44 | 2.3 |\n| 069 init | 5.05 | 0.76 | 6.7 |\n| 069 step128 | 0.97 | 0.61 | 1.6 |\n\nThe regression gradient collapses about 5x while the ranking gradient barely moves, so by step 128 ranking already shapes the MLP update more than at init. With the global clip of 1.0 binding every step and AdamW per-element normalisation, detaching regression would not release a suppressed signal. It would remove the only absolute anchor, change the shared clip coefficient for A/C, and hand the whole per-element step to the noisier term, exactly as both critics argued. Centroid detach should be recorded as KILL rather than \"on hold\". These are local first-B64 observations at two states; they do not prove alignment on other batches or on R@1-wrong anchors, but the proposal's premise was a general conflict claim and it fails where it was tested.\n\n## 2. What actually bounds the held-panel R@1\n\nFrom the query-transition diagnostic: per seed, 45 queries are wrong under both arms, 11 to 12 are fixed, 5 to 6 are broken. Jointly across seeds, 9 queries are fixed in both, 5 broken in both, 1714 unchanged. The candidate's +0.35pp is a net +6 queries riding on \u00b117 churn around an untouched core, and the mAP gain comes from secondary positives on already-correct queries, which is what SmoothAP rewards.\n\nThe frozen product lower-bound gate needs roughly +8 net queries per seed at the observed 0.91pp interval width. Effects in this recipe family are 0.3pp on this panel and the older lineage's 106-error core was invariant across width, depth, budget and label-granularity arms. So the panel is underpowered for this family, and a pass by two more queries would be noise on a panel already used for the KILL. No gradient-routing, schedule or budget change can be expected to clear it without touching the core, and nothing yet measures whether the core is touchable.\n\n## 3. Chosen next action: zero-training core-error census, with a pre-registered branch\n\nRun a CPU-only census over the four accepted export receipts (control/candidate x two seeds, exact packed codes for the 1734 query and 1715 gallery rows), recomputing the full packed score matrix per arm under the deployed scorer semantics. Let K_near be the number of core queries with best-positive rank 2 under all four arms whose impostor is not a mutual pair.\n\n- K_near < 8 per seed: no new training arm in this family. Go serving-first with the checkpoint selected by the already-frozen rule (control), and spend DGX on the unqualified native parity, lifecycle and matched B1/B32 latency panel, then a single sealed official In-Shop read.\n- K_near \u2265 8 per seed: the one admissible arm is data coverage, FIT scope 1008 products / 6355 rows \u2192 all non-held train products (about 3000 products, 19k rows). It is the only axis untested in this lineage and the only TRAIN-only change that raises impostor density for unseen products. Matched controls: same initializer fit procedure on the new scope, same four-tensor candidate vs A/C control, same seeds, batches, clip, optimizer, scorer and panel. Its stop rule is the unchanged frozen gate, and the census count is a necessary condition, not a prediction of benefit.\n\nCost. The census is CPU-only, minutes, no DGX, no new data. The data-coverage arm, if triggered, is about 5 DGX-hours on measured precedents (four TRAIN arms at 2.2 to 2.35 ks, four exports at 1.3 ks, score at 0.56 ks, plus initializer fit, CPU600 and mechanics, all unmeasured at 3x rows) plus a new scope contract, because 6355, 1008/2016 and 12 singletons are hard-coded in both trainers and the connected contract pins CONTROL1008/6355.\n\nRequired source APIs: the extracted serving package's load_inference/inference_outputs and exact packed top-k semantics for score recomputation, ranking_membership for product grouping, the product-transition diagnostic's SHA-bound partition for identities, and the four export receipts (6 MB each) as the only inputs.\n\n## 4. Uncertainties and what precedes official confirmation\n\nUnverified: that the export receipts carry per-row packed codes and image paths. The v4 vectors cover one batch; the subset test on R@1-wrong anchors proposed by the research critic remains the only cheap reopen condition for routing ideas, and I do not recommend running it unless the census shows a reachable core. Before any official read: checkpoint selection frozen on TRAIN identities by the existing rule, serving parity and latency qualified, and the read labelled exploratory versus confirmatory.
